originality.rationale: Dejter (arXiv:1002.1960) establishes the exceptional Klein graph via Coxeter/Heawood hexagon geometry but does not identify its vertices as 24 Heawood perfect matchings with single alternating-hexagon adjacency. A public Heawood graph table contains the 24 perfect-matching and eight three-factorization counts, and a Klein graph database contains the known 24-by-24 adjacency matrix, without an isomorphism of the matching-flip graph. Direct checking of 576 adjacency entries establishes that new bridge. Existing resonance/flip edge counts alone do not imply this labelled isomorphism or the exact distance-intersection rule; no covering result was identified among the inspected materials. Residual unindexed-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed graph-transformation, one-factorization, or Klein-map literature might contain an equivalent correspondence.
Some earlier exact hexagon-flip counts may overlap the computed 84 edges, though counts do not imply this graph identification.
The published 24-vertex Klein adjacency is treated as a reliable primary graph reference; it is not rederived from a topological embedding.

value.rationale: The Fano-plane incidence graph and Klein distance-regular graph are canonical and independently motivated. Their unexpected exact correspondence via 6-cycle perfect-matching reconfiguration yields a global optimal flip-distance rule and explains the eight three-edge-colourings as antipodal triples in a threefold cover of K8. This is structural information not recoverable from a bare 24-state count or routine invariant tabulation.
